name: PT Rockfields Properti Indonesia Tbk.

frontmatter.title: Rockfields Properti: a sound rent roll at a konglo price
frontmatter.summary: Rockfields owns a single Grade-A Jakarta office tower let at close to 90.0%, plus two paused projects. The rent roll is sound; the price is not. RNAV is Rp378 and a rent-roll DCF Rp483, a twelve-month fundamental of Rp418 against Rp1,995, and the konglo lens sets a Rp1,440 target: SELL, -27.8% total return.
thesis: The business is a landlord, not a developer: every rupiah of FY2025 and FY2024 revenue is office rent, service charge, utilities, parking or fit-out, with no development-sales line and no marketing-sales KPI [S14].

Restating D&A from the LK turns profit into a cash story: 34.3 of building depreciation sits inside cost of revenue, so EBITDA is 74.1 on 136.1 of revenue, against the data pack's understated charge [S14, S0].

RNAV is Rp378 a share - the tower capitalised on its own post-depreciation income at the like-for-like office cap rate, plus the development land at a stated haircut, less net debt - and the rent-roll DCF is Rp483; the blend is a Rp418 twelve-month fundamental against Rp1,995 [S14, S0].

The premium is a konglo phenomenon, not an earnings one: the exchange's HSC measure shows almost the entire register in a few hands, HSC names left the IHSG calculation on 13 November 2026, and MSCI has frozen Indonesian index increases while it consults on Standalone status [S7, S16, S17].
The twelve-month price is set by how much of that premium compresses, not by the rent roll: base Rp1,242, bear Rp635, bull Rp2,640, target Rp1,440 against Rp1,995 [S16, S17, S0].

catalysts.event: Convertible loan from PT Pohon Berkat Gemilang matures; the convertible note sets conversion at nominal value on the {{fact.F26|money}} principal outstanding, so repayment or conversion is a per-share event [S14]
FY2026 audited results, the first full-year test of the rent roll after the share-price move [S14]
Deadline for the raised free-float minimum; ROCK reports {{mkt.free_float_pct}} on the IDX registry, so the question is index eligibility, not compliance [S19]
MSCI decision on moving Indonesia to Standalone status after the consultation closes [S17]
Quarterly IHSG review, the earliest date the HSC exclusion could be revisited [S16]

blocks.text: Rockfields Properti is a boutique Jakarta office landlord that the market has spent two years pricing as a development story. The FY2025 audited accounts settle what it is: 136.1 of revenue, office rent the largest line at IDR82.9bn, with service charge, utilities, overtime, telephone, parking and fit-out making up the rest, and no development-sales line in either FY2025 or FY2024 [S14]. The company owns the Noble House tower in Mega Kuningan and, through subsidiaries, two development sites whose construction stopped when management amended the development plan [S14]. There are no marketing sales to underwrite, no handover cycle and no landbank release schedule: this is a rent roll with a stranded project attached.

The rent roll is not the problem. Occupancy is close to 90.0% and management describes the resulting cash flow as stable [S2]. The problem is the price. Our RNAV is Rp378 a share: the tower is capitalised on its own post-depreciation income at a cap rate matched to the office peer set, the development book enters at a stated haircut to carrying cost, and net debt and minorities are deducted [S14, S0]. A rent-roll DCF gives Rp483, and the blend is a twelve-month fundamental value of Rp418. At Rp1,995 the shares sit at 5.34x our value today of Rp373 [S0].

Why the gap exists is the whole case. ROCK sits on the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration list with almost the entire register in the hands of a small group of investors [S7, S18], against a 20.0% registry free float [S0]. HSC names were removed from the IHSG calculation from 13 November 2026, and MSCI has frozen index increases for Indonesian names while it consults on Standalone status [S16, S17]. In that regime the price is a premium to fundamentals, and our konglo base case assumes only part of it closes - which is how a fundamental value of Rp418 becomes a Rp1,440 target and a -27.8% total return: SELL.

Two things would move the value. Downside: the convertible's IDR45.0bn outstanding matures in December 2026, the convertible note sets conversion at par, and the paused Rasuna Said project needs capital the balance sheet can no longer borrow cheaply [S14]. Upside: a restart with a signed tenant would convert 397 IDR bn of sunk cost from a balance-sheet question mark into a second income asset. Neither is in the base case; both are in the scenarios.

Rockfields is a holding company for five subsidiaries, each holding one property or one project [S11]. The group presents itself as a developer of high-yielding, premium investment properties and lists Noble House in Mega Kuningan among its completed assets [S6, S9]. The consolidated P&L is nevertheless a single-asset rent roll: the tower is the only investment property on the balance sheet, carried at cost less depreciation at 428 IDR bn, and it produced essentially all of the group's revenue [S14].

Revenue composition is unambiguous. The revenue note splits the year into office rent IDR82.9bn of the IDR136.1bn total, then service charge, utilities, overtime, telephone, internet, parking, fit-out and a small other line [S14]. There is no development-sales line and no marketing-sales KPI; the fit-out and room-installation line is IDR0.6bn and is the only project-based revenue in the accounts [S14]. The company profile speaks of 495,700 sqm of developing floor area across the subsidiaries, but that is floor area, not a land bank, and it is not earning [S11].

The development book is where the balance sheet gets interesting. Two projects sit in investment property under development at 397 IDR bn: the International Exchange House site on Rasuna Said in Kuningan and the Azerai Bali site in Ungasan, Badung [S14]. A further 49.3 IDR bn of undeveloped land sits in Kebon Jeruk, West Jakarta [S14]. During FY2025 management amended the project development plan so that no further construction activity takes place, and reclassified 400 IDR bn of construction in progress out of fixed assets into investment property under development [S14]. That is the accounting signature of a paused project, not a pipeline.

The convertible is the one instrument that can change the share count. The convertible note says the IDR45.0bn outstanding after the partial repayment converts into new shares at nominal value on the December 2026 maturity, and the nominal value is Rp50 [S14]. Conversion therefore issues shares at par, not at the market price; the base case assumes repayment because the terms require issuer and shareholder approval and management has already repaid part of the facility, and the dilution case is carried in the scenarios and the valuation bridge [S14].

Strategy, as management tells it, is to restart. In December 2025 the company announced accelerated repayment of its bank facility, pointed to occupancy close to 90.0% and described a pipeline including a new Rasuna Said project and Bali, with a new funding facility to be decided in management [S2]. The same presentation described ROCK as a developer with no debt, its own equity and a strategic landbank [S2]. The bank loan was indeed repaid in full during FY2025, leaving the convertible as the only material borrowing [S14].

Competitive position is niche, not leading. ROCK is a sub-scale Jakarta CBD landlord: one tower of 83,970 sqm of building, 51.0 employees, and no fee business beyond managing its own asset [S14, S0]. Its edge, such as it is, is the location and quality of a single building, not scale, brand or land access.

The relevant frame is Jakarta's office market, not the residential market the template usually addresses. Demand comes from CBD corporate tenants, supply from towers completed in the last cycle, and pricing from a rupiah rent per square metre that has been broadly flat in nominal terms while costs rise. For a single-asset landlord the variables that matter are occupancy, the escalation written into leases, service-charge recovery and the cap rate at which the building would trade. ROCK reports occupancy close to 90.0% [S2]; everything else has to be inferred from the accounts, which is why the valuation leans on the LK's own income and depreciation rather than an industry rent index.

The macro backdrop does not help. The house deck has the BI rate at 5.8 rate spot and 5.8 rate in FY2027E, CPI at 3.3 rate and USD/IDR at Rp18,350/USD, with the macro desk in a balance-of-payments-pressure regime that tilts rate-sensitive Indonesian assets to avoid [S0]. Higher-for-longer rates raise the discount rate on a long-duration rent stream, widen office cap rates and make the convertible refinancing harder. Revenue is commercial rent, so mortgage transmission matters less than for a residential developer; the discount rate does not.

The property cycle has been weak. Press coverage through 2026 describes sluggish listed-developer performance into the third quarter, and the market's verdict on small property names has been brutal [S0]. The konglo cohort in particular has given back most of its post-listing gains [S0]. ROCK's own shares ranged from 426.0 to 3,770.0 and back to 1,995.0 over the trailing year, a range unconnected to rent [S0].

Regulation cuts both ways. The building sits on a Hak Guna Bangunan title expiring in 2041, so the asset has a finite life and the land will need extension or renewal; the Rasuna Said land title runs to 2033 [S14]. On the market side the exchange adopted a revised HSC methodology on 11 November 2026 - ten holders or fewer controlling the overwhelming majority of the register, with no market-cap floor - which took the list to 383 emiten, and it removed HSC names from the IHSG calculation from 13 November 2026 [S18, S16]. The exchange also put the raised minimum free float into force with deadlines from March 2027 [S19]. ROCK's 20.0% registry float is above the new minimum [S0]; the binding constraints are the HSC status and the index exclusions, which decide who can own the stock.

Five forces, briefly. Supplier power is low: contractors and service providers compete for one building's work. Buyer power is moderate and rising, because corporate tenants can consolidate into newer space and negotiate service charges. New entry in Mega Kuningan is constrained by land scarcity, but substitute space in newer submarkets is plentiful. Rivalry is high and structural against a large stock of competing Grade-A space. Substitutes - co-working and decentralised offices - are a slow threat. The result is pricing power only at the margin, which is why the valuation rests on capitalised income rather than growth [S0].

Reported profit understates the cash economics, and that adjustment is the most important number in the model. The data pack shows FY2025 D&A of 34.3 before restatement; the LK charges 34.3 IDR bn of building depreciation to cost of revenue alone [S14, S0]. Restated, EBITDA is 74.1 on 136.1 of revenue, a 54.5% margin, against EBIT of 39.8 [S14]. The engine rebuilds history from these facts and every forecast ratio here uses the restated base.

Revenue grew 14.0% to 136.1 in FY2025 from 119.4, driven by rent and service charge [S14]. Gross margin reached 52.4% as rent grew against largely fixed property costs; operating expenses were 31.5 and EBIT margin 29.2% [S14]. Net profit to parent was 26.1, or 18.2 a share [S14]. FY2026E revenue is 140.8, growth of 3.5%, with nine-month 2026 revenue running ahead of the prior year and first-half profit of 15.7 IDR bn [S0, S4].

The forecast is deliberately boring because the business is. Recurring revenue grows in the low-to-mid single digits, inside the macro deck's CPI and consistent with contracted escalations at occupancy close to 90.0% [S0, S2]. Gross margin is 51.6% in FY2026E: that is the nine-month 2026 ratio plus the fourth-quarter uplift the prior year actually delivered, because the nine-month 2025 comparative was lower than the FY2025 rate and the fourth quarter carried a higher margin, so carrying the raw nine-month ratio into the full year would understate the base case [S0]. SG&A stays at the FY2025 ratio with no cost programme assumed [S14]. There is no development revenue in the forecast, no land sales and no new tower.

Cash generation is the strength. FY2025 free cash flow to the firm was 54.0 against net profit of 26.1 - accruals are negative, the opposite of the earnings-quality warning sign - because depreciation is large and tenants pay in advance [S14]. Unearned revenue of 26.4 IDR bn is a structural funding source [S14]. Capex was 2.2, maintenance only; development capex sits in the paused project, not in the cash-flow line [S14].

The balance sheet is the unusual part. Equity is 820.5 against total assets of 935 IDR bn, but the parent carries an accumulated deficit, so book equity is paid-in capital, not retained profit [S14]. Cash was 36.9 IDR bn at December 2025 with net debt of 7.9, all of it the convertible and small consumer-financing balances, because the bank facility was repaid in full [S14]. By September 2026 the group had moved to a net cash position [S0]. Net gearing is negligible and there is no dollar debt, so the balance sheet is not the risk; the maturity is.

Capital allocation has been conservative to a fault. Payout is 0.0 and no dividend has been paid in the price history [S0, S14]; the accumulated deficit means none is distributable without a capital reduction. Cash has gone into the tower, the paused projects and bank repayment. The convertible is the one instrument that could dilute: the convertible note sets conversion at nominal value, so conversion would issue shares at par and take the count from 1,435.2m to well above two billion; the base case assumes repayment, and the dilution is quantified in section four [S14].

Earnings-quality flags, run through the house card. Accruals: negative, no issue. Divergence: receivables grew slower than revenue and related-party receivables were immaterial, so no channel-stuffing flag [S14]. IDX regime: ROCK is on the HSC list and out of the main indices - a manipulation-class gate for index money even though it is a disclosure status, not a finding of wrongdoing [S18, S7, S16]. Structure: a concentrated register, a third-party convertible, a paused project reclassified rather than impaired, and no dividend [S14, S7]. The reclassification deserves its own flag: moving 400 IDR bn of construction in progress into investment property under development after amending the plan avoids the impairment test a construction asset would face, and the write-down booked against it was small relative to the carrying value [S14]. That is optics-class and disclosed, but it says the project is worth less than the book.

The method set fits the asset, not the sector label. ROCK has no presales, so a developer's presales roll-forward is empty; what it has is a rent roll and a book of land. We weight RNAV at 70% and a rent-roll DCF at 30%, with RNAV primary. The own-history P/E and P/BV cross-checks appear in the valuation table as market context only and carry no weight: they are prices of the same stock in the same konglo regime, so putting them inside the fundamental would embed the premium the lens then prices a second time. The discount rate is the house COE build: the risk-free rate 7.4% less the sovereign default spread 1.6%, plus levered beta 0.91 applied to the sum of the mature equity risk premium 4.2% and the country risk premium 2.5%, giving COE 11.9% and WACC 11.9% [S0]. That is the rate a single-asset Jakarta landlord should clear in a balance-of-payments-pressure regime.

The RNAV is built from the LK line by line. The tower is capitalised on its own gross profit of 71.3 at a cap rate set at the top of the like-for-like office peer set on the engine's identical base - the peers' implied yields run from the mid-single digits to a low double digit on the same post-depreciation gross profit, and the earlier draft's private-basis conversion to a pre-depreciation yield was not like-for-like and is dropped [S14, S0]. The development book enters at a stated haircut of thirty per cent to cost - 397 IDR bn of investment property under development plus 49.3 IDR bn of land for development - because construction is paused, no appraisal exists, the company itself impaired the book, and the Jakarta land-price cross-check (Rp16,224,082/sqm against 11,968 sqm of Rasuna Said land) puts the site below its carrying cost [S14, S8]. Net debt and minorities are deducted at the latest balance sheet [S0]. The result is a method value of Rp378 a share after the target discount to RNAV.

The DCF is an independent cross-check, not a second copy of the RNAV. It discounts the rent roll's free cash flow to the firm at the house WACC with a terminal growth rate and gives Rp483, 27.6% above the RNAV; the gap is the property-band discount. The RNAV applies the house discount to asset value because IDX developers trade below NAV, while the DCF has no such discount and 49.1% of its value is terminal. That terminal share rests on a perpetuity, and the perpetuity in turn assumes the HGB title on the tower (expiring 2 December 2041, F18) is renewed: the LK discloses the expiry and the certificate but no extension premium, no renewal cost and no statement of management's intent, so the model carries renewal at no explicit cost [S14]. The exposure is bounded, not eliminated: the perpetuity sits in the DCF, which carries 30% of the blend, while the primary RNAV values the land and the capitalised income without a horizon, and the sensitivity grid prices the RNAV discount, which is where the value actually sits. We keep RNAV primary because the market clears property assets at a discount to appraisal value, and we keep the DCF at a weight because a buyer of the rent roll would underwrite its cash flow, not its book.

The discount is the contested number and we took the top of the house band. ROCK's P/B was well below book in FY2022-FY2024, before the re-rating, and against RNAV that history maps to a wider discount than the one we apply [S0]. We stay at the top of the band because the tower is close to full occupancy, the balance sheet is in net cash and the asset is Grade-A [S2, S0]. A tighter discount would be a re-rating dressed as valuation; a wider one would ignore the quality of the rent roll.

The market cross-checks disagree with the fundamental, and the disagreement is the point. ROCK trades at 109.5x next year's earnings and 3.4x book, far above asset value, because it has traded at a high multiple in every year of the price history [S0]. Those are not evidence the business is worth more; they are evidence the stock has persistently traded above asset value, which is exactly what the konglo lens is built to price. That is why they carry no weight in the blend: a triple-digit multiple on a no-growth rent roll with no dividend is a regime price, not a fundamental one. We show it, explain it and keep it out of the value.

The convertible's dilution is in the bridge as a probability-weighted cost, and it does not reach both methods. The engine applies bridge items to the cash-flow and sum-of-the-parts legs; the property-RNAV method prices the assets off the balance-sheet share count and carries no per-share bridge. So the blend absorbs the conversion cost at the DCF weight, not at full weight: on a full-weight carry the fundamental would be more than a tenth lower and the twelve-month value would fall toward the base regime scenario, Rp1,242, rather than Rp1,440 [S14]. We state the treatment rather than hide it, and the rating is SELL on either figure.

What the price implies is the cleanest way to say it. At Rp1,995 the market pays 3.4x book and 37.7x restated EBITDA [S0]. For the rent roll to justify that, the tower would have to be worth several times its capitalised income, or rents would have to rise sharply with occupancy held. Nothing in the documents we hold supports either path. The price is a premium to value today of 5.34x - value today being Rp373, against the twelve-month fundamental of Rp418 - and the konglo lens is the only framework in the house that explains why such a premium persists and how it decays.

That lens is not a view about wrongdoing. HSC status is a concentrated-ownership disclosure, not a finding against the company [S18]. What it does is remove the stock from the IHSG calculation, freeze MSCI index increases for Indonesian names and leave a 20.0% float in a register where almost everything is held by a group [S7, S16, S17, S0]. The deck adds a small premium adjustment for HSC membership and then compresses the observed premium by a scenario-specific fraction: 35.0% in the base case, 75.0% in the bear and -10.0% in the bull. Applied to ROCK, the lens's own base regime case targets Rp1,242, its bear Rp635 and its bull Rp2,640; the probability-weighted result is Rp1,440 [S16, S17, S0].

The central risk is not that the rent roll deteriorates; it is that the premium paid for it stays where it is. Our fundamental value is Rp418 and the shares are at Rp1,995, so any scenario in which the konglo premium compresses faster than the deck assumes produces a larger loss than our target implies. That is the honest way to state a SELL on a name whose downside depends on other investors' behaviour as much as on the company's cash flow.

Regulatory and index risk is first-order. ROCK is on the HSC list, out of the IHSG calculation and the main indices, and exposed to the MSCI consultation that could move Indonesia to Standalone [S16, S17, S18]. It reports 20.0% on the IDX registry against the raised minimum [S0, S19]; the issue is that index-driven demand cannot return while the stock is excluded. Likelihood: high that the exclusion persists through the next review. Impact: high on the premium, low on cash flow.

Liquidity is the risk the register creates, and it is measurable. Three-month average daily traded value is IDR0.6bn against a market capitalisation of IDR2,863.2bn, so the stock turns over a tiny fraction of its value each day [S0]. A position equal to a hundredth of the company would take months of the entire daily volume at realistic participation; a position equal to a tenth would take more than a year of the entire daily volume at full participation and several years at any realistic participation. That is why the house applies a ten per cent liquidity discount, and it is also why a small flow moves the price. The register is described as 99.8% held by a group of investors [S7], while the pack shows 80.0% insider ownership and a 20.0% float [S0]; the two measures disagree on the identity of the holders, and no holder above five per cent is named in the material we hold, which is itself a transparency gap. The float is not a liquid float in any practical sense.

Balance-sheet and liquidity risk is second. The convertible's IDR45.0bn outstanding matures in December 2026 [S14]. Repayment from cash is affordable at the September position, but it would consume most of the liquid buffer and leave the Rasuna Said restart unfunded. Conversion is the contract's default if the issuer approves it: the convertible note sets conversion at nominal value, Rp50 a share, so the outstanding principal would issue new shares at par and raise the share count by roughly three-fifths, a transfer from existing holders to the lender that would cut per-share asset value by more than a third. The base case assumes repayment because approval is required and management has already repaid part of the facility; the dilution is carried as a probability-weighted cost in the valuation bridge, which enters the blend at the DCF weight only (section four sets out the full-weight figure), so it is a disclosed partial carry in the fundamental, not a full one.

Operational risk is concentrated. One building produces all the revenue, occupancy is close to 90.0% [S2], and the title runs to 2041 [S14]. A large tenant leaving, a service-charge dispute or a building-system failure hits revenue directly; extending the land right is a terminal-value question we cannot price today. Likelihood: low in any one year. Impact: high.

Development risk is the upside and the downside in the same asset. 397 IDR bn of cost sits in two paused projects, reclassified rather than written down, with only a small impairment [S14]. Restarting Rasuna Said needs capital and a tenant; leaving it paused means the carrying value is a hope. Likelihood of a restart within twelve months: low. Impact: high either way.

Governance and structure risk carries the most weight on the price. A concentrated register, a 20.0% float, a founder-controlled board and no dividend [S7, S0] mean minority holders have no mechanism to force the value out. Related-party flows are small, so this is not a related-party extraction story; it is a control-and-float story [S14].

Macro and FX risk is modest. Revenue is rupiah, debt is rupiah and dollar balances are small [S14]. The deck's USD/IDR path of Rp18,350/USD and BI rate of 5.8 rate matter through the discount rate and the convertible, not through translation [S0].

The three business scenarios mirror the same four drivers - recurring growth, recurring gross margin, cap rate and RNAV discount - moved by equal and opposite amounts, and they contain no index or MSCI events: the regime runs its own scenarios in the konglo lens, and pricing it in both places would count it twice. The base case (45.0%) holds the forecast path and compresses the konglo premium as the deck does, giving Rp459. The bear case (30.0%) takes growth and margin down, widens the cap rate and the RNAV discount, and marks a book that already sits below cost at a harsher value: Rp310. The bull case (25.0%) mirrors those shocks, restarts Rasuna Said with a signed tenant and narrows the discount: Rp659. The probabilities are the analyst's, written in the assumptions file, not the engine's.

The rating is sensitive to one deck parameter. The base regime scenario at Rp1,242 and the bear at Rp635 are below the current price; only the bull regime at Rp2,640 clears it. The base case assumes the lens closes 35.0% of the log gap in twelve months, and the parameter is not something the company controls. A materially smaller compression would leave the target level with today's price and make the name a HOLD, and that would need a named flow catalyst inside the window - index re-inclusion, a large float increase with an identified buyer, or MSCI retaining Indonesia in Emerging Markets. None is dated before the convertible maturity, and the deck's own flag logic raises the compression when a free-float step falls due, so a float increase is not a bull case for the target; it speeds the closing of the premium rather than preserving it.

The strongest case against us is simple and we state it plainly. ROCK has been expensive on P/E for years and the market has repeatedly paid up for the story [S0]. If the konglo premium is a permanent feature of this register - if the float never widens, the exclusion is irrelevant to the holders and the company restarts Rasuna Said on its own equity - then our fundamental value is the wrong anchor and the bull case of Rp2,640 is the right one. We do not think that is the most likely path, because the exchange's own rules, the MSCI consultation and the convertible maturity all point the other way within twelve months; but it is a real path, and it is why the rating is SELL rather than something stronger.

Signposts that would change the view: a conversion of the loan at a price near book; a named tenant for the Rasuna Said restart; a free-float increase that restored index eligibility; an MSCI decision to keep Indonesia in Emerging Markets; or an impairment of the development book. The first four would move us toward the bull case; the fifth would confirm the bear.

Ownership is the defining fact. The exchange's HSC table shows ROCK with 99.8% of the register held by a group of investors, the highest concentration on the list, against a 20.0% free float on the IDX registry and an insider holding of 80.0% in the data pack [S7, S0]. The company was founded in 2013, listed in 2020 and is run by its founder, with a president commissioner, a financial director and a corporate secretary [S6, S0]. The two measures are not reconciled by any source we hold, and no holder above five per cent is named: the beneficial owners behind the group are not disclosed in the material. The register is why the stock behaves as it does.

Related-party exposure is small but present. Trade receivables from related parties were immaterial at the last year-end, and payments to related parties in financing activities were a small fraction of operating cash flow [S14]. There is no disclosed loan to or from an affiliate, no guarantee to a controlling shareholder's other ventures and no discounted placement to affiliates in the period covered. The convertible lender, PT Pohon Berkat Gemilang, is described in the LK as a third party [S14].

Structure flags, classified. Manipulation-class: none found - we checked the HSC status, the index exclusions, related-party balances, the convertible and the reclassification, and found no fabricated cash or fictitious revenue. Optics-class, disclosed: the reclassification of construction in progress into investment property under development after the development plan was amended, with only a small impairment [S14]; the zero-coupon convertible that matures inside twelve months [S14]; the absence of any dividend despite positive cash generation [S0]; and the concentrated register that leaves minority holders without a vote that matters [S7].

Board and audit. The company reports a president director, a financial director, a head of internal audit and a corporate secretary and files audited consolidated statements [S0, S14]. We have seen no qualification of the opinion in the material reviewed and make no claim beyond that; the one accounting judgement that matters - the paused project - is disclosed rather than hidden [S14].

Dividend record is nil. Payout is 0.0 in every year of the price history and the parent's accumulated deficit leaves no distributable reserve [S0, S14]. For a landlord this is a capital-allocation choice, not a cash constraint: the business generates 54.0 of free cash flow to the firm and holds 26.4 IDR bn of rent received in advance [S14]. Minority holders receive nothing while the controlling group decides where the cash goes.

ESG exposures are ordinary for a single-office landlord: building energy and water efficiency, tenant health and safety, and the land-title and community questions around the Bali site. The tower is insured against earthquake, terrorism, sabotage and fire [S14]. There is no disclosed emissions target, no sustainability report in the material reviewed and no green financing. On governance, the concentration and the index exclusion are the ESG issues that matter to a portfolio, and they are covered above.

The dated catalysts are few and all about the regime rather than the rent. The convertible matures in December 2026 [S14]. In March 2027 the raised free-float minimum comes into force, and ROCK's 20.0% is compliant, so the question is index eligibility rather than compliance [S19]. MSCI feedback closes in April 2027 and the decision follows by June 2027 [S17]. Each quarterly IHSG review is a date on which the HSC exclusion could be revisited [S16].

The operating catalysts are slower. FY2026 audited results will show whether the nine-month revenue trend held through the fourth quarter [S0, S4]. Any announcement on the Rasuna Said restart, with a named tenant or a funding facility, would be the largest positive event available, because it would convert 397 IDR bn of carrying value into a second income stream [S14, S2]. Any impairment of that book, or a conversion of the loan at a low price, is the mirror image.

The KPIs we watch are short. Occupancy of the tower, close to 90.0% [S2]. Rent per square metre and service-charge recovery, both derivable from the revenue note [S14]. Free cash flow against net profit, to confirm negative accruals persist [S14]. The convertible balance and any conversion announcement [S14]. Free float and the HSC designation, both published by the exchange [S16, S18, S19]. And the discount to RNAV, the variable to which the target is most sensitive [S0].

Rockfields is a small Indonesian office landlord whose history sits inside the broader story of Jakarta's commercial property cycle: a tower completed in the middle of the last office upcycle, a pandemic that emptied it, and a recovery in occupancy that has not been matched by a recovery in rents. Its listing came during a period when small property developers were marketed to retail investors on land-bank narratives rather than cash flow. That background explains why the shares can trade far from asset value without any single event causing it, and why the exchange's concentration rules matter more to this name than to a large, widely held developer.

bear.narrative: Office demand softens with the economy: occupancy slips from the 90% management reports (F16), the service-charge and utility recovery weakens, rents escalate below CPI, and the paused Rasuna Said restart needs capex the balance sheet cannot fund without new debt. The convertible matures in December 2026; if the issuer approves conversion at par the share count rises by about 63% (F26, F27), and if it is repaid from cash the liquidity buffer is gone. With no dividend and no development sales the only support is the rent roll, so the cap rate on Noble House widens and the discount to RNAV widens with it. This is a business case only: the index and MSCI regime is priced separately in the konglo lens.

bull.narrative: Jakarta CBD office demand recovers and the company executes: occupancy moves from the 90% management reports (F16) toward the mid-90s, rents escalate faster than CPI, and the Rasuna Said project restarts with a signed tenant so the Rp342.8bn of sunk cost becomes a second income asset and the 495,700 sqm of developing floor area (F17) starts to earn. The cap rate tightens toward the 6.0% a single Grade-A tower with a long lease profile would fetch, and the discount to RNAV narrows toward the bottom of the name's own band. The convertible is repaid rather than converted, so the share count stays at 1,435m. This is a business case only: the index and MSCI regime is priced separately in the konglo lens, and a free-float step due inside the window raises the lens's compression rather than lowering it.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs presales growth and RNAV discount

adjustments.why: on the exchange's HSC list (as of 2026-11-11): out of the IHSG, the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and the MSCI indexes [konglo deck S26]

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Presales growth
assumptions.basis: Zero in every year: there are no marketing sales to grow. Note 27 of the FY2025 LK (F1) lists rent, service charge, utilities, overtime, telephone, parking, fit-out and other revenue and no development-sales line in either year, so the presales line carries only the fit-out seed (F22) and is held flat. The stalled projects are carried in landbank_value at cost instead.

assumptions.label: Share of presales recognised in the same year
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0: with no presales the recognition share only matters as a mechanical pass-through, and rent and service income is recognised as it is earned rather than on handover. Keeping it at the engine default of 0.5 would halve a revenue base that has no handover lag at all.

assumptions.label: Recurring revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 3.0%: nine months of 2026 revenue of Rp103.45bn (S0 quarterly) against Rp99.66bn for the same nine months of 2025 is 3.8%, and the first half grew 3.1% to Rp69.18bn (S4), so the year is tracking to about 3% with the fourth quarter at the 2025 level. Then 5%, 5%, 4.5%, 4.5% a year: contracted office escalations of roughly 4-5% on 90% occupancy (F16), inside the house deck's 3.28% CPI, with no new tower assumed until the Rasuna Said project is actually restarted. Terminal growth 4%.

assumptions.label: Development gross margin
assumptions.basis: Inert while dev_revenue is zero, but set at 20% rather than left empty so the template has a coherent value if the International Exchange House or Azerai Bali projects are ever completed and sold. Twenty percent is a plain developer margin on Jakarta commercial product; nothing in the filings supports a specific number because there is no development P&L to calibrate against.

assumptions.label: Recurring gross margin
assumptions.basis: FY2025 actual 52.4% (gross profit Rp71.329bn on revenue Rp136.119bn, F1) after Rp34.34bn of building depreciation in cost of revenue. FY2026E 51.7% is the nine-month 2026 ratio (Rp52.37bn of gross profit on Rp103.45bn of revenue, 50.6%) plus the Q4 seasonal uplift the prior year actually delivered: 9M-2025 was 51.3% (Rp51.13bn of gross profit on Rp99.66bn of revenue, S0 quarterly) against a 55.4% fourth quarter, so carrying the raw nine-month 50.6% into the full year would understate the base case by about a point. Then 52.0% and 52.4% as rent escalates against largely fixed property costs, back to the last actual and no further. No margin expansion beyond the last actual: utilities and service charge are pass-through and management has not announced any cost programme.

assumptions.label: Cap rate for investment property (RNAV)
assumptions.basis: 7.5% on accounting gross profit, which is post Rp34.34bn of building depreciation (F5). It is the top of the like-for-like office peer range on the engine's identical base (MKPI 7.5%, RDTX 8.5%, ARGO 9.0%) and the most generous point in that set for the subject. The superseded 6.0% was a conversion to a pre-depreciation yield, a basis the peers do not use, so it is dropped; no source in the filings quotes a cap rate, so the rate is a house judgement anchored on the LK's own income and depreciation, and it is the single most important number in the RNAV (sensitivity 6.0-8.5%).

assumptions.label: Target discount to RNAV
assumptions.basis: 60%: the top of the house 40-70% band for IDX developers and just inside the name's own history. ROCK's P/B was 0.50-0.69x in FY2022-FY2024 (S0 history multiples) against RNAV of about 2x book, which maps to a 65-75% discount; the tight end of the band is justified by net cash, 90% occupancy and a single Grade-A asset, not by the current price. The stock trades at 3.5x book today, so the discount is a de-rating assumption, not a re-rating one.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 23.2%, the FY2025 actual (Rp31.536bn of operating expenses on Rp136.119bn of revenue, F1) and the three-year average. Held flat: there is no disclosed cost programme and SG&A is mostly staff and building management, which grows with rent.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK, not from the data pack: FY2025 investment-property depreciation of Rp34.340bn (F5) is 25.2% of revenue, against the pack's Rp1.09bn. The charge is fixed in rupiah (straight-line on the Noble House tower to the 2041 HGB expiry), so it falls as a percentage as revenue grows: 24.5% in FY2026E down to 20.2% in FY2030E.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: 1.3%, the three-year average and the FY2025 actual (Rp2.246bn): maintenance capex on the tower. Excludes any restart of the Rasuna Said construction, which would be a balance-sheet project and is the main upside/downside swing not in the base case.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: -12.6%, the three-year average: tenants pay rent in advance (unearned revenue Rp26.444bn, F13) while the group carries almost no inventory, so working capital is a source of cash and scales with rent. No change assumed.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 33.5%, the FY2025 effective rate (tax Rp13.162bn on pre-tax profit Rp39.280bn). The company is taxed on commercial rent and service income at the standard corporate rate with no final-tax regime visible in the LK, so the reported rate is carried forward.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 3.0%: the only borrowings are the Rp42.250bn convertible from PT Pohon Berkat Gemilang, which pays a 0% coupon (note 21), plus small consumer-financing balances, against FY2025 interest expense of Rp1.157bn on opening debt of Rp89.4bn. The convertible matures in December 2026, so the rate only applies to one year of the forecast.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 2.0%, the three-year average of interest income on opening cash (FY2025 Rp0.704bn on Rp27.1bn); rupiah deposits.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: management repaid the Bank Mandiri facility in full during 2025 (note 18) and describes the company as debt-free apart from the convertible, with a new facility only "decided together in management" (S2). No new borrowing is assumed until a facility is signed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: no recurring non-operating income or charge is disclosed. FX is immaterial - cash is held in rupiah with only small dollar balances (note 5).

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero: the non-controlling interest is Rp-85.8m in total and the subsidiaries are 99.99% owned (note 1), so minorities take none of profit.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. No dividend has been paid in any year of the price history (S0) and the parent carries an accumulated deficit of Rp99.528bn against paid-in capital of Rp847.0bn, so there is no distributable reserve. A dividend would require either a capital reduction or years of profit; none is assumed.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero in the base share count, because the base case assumes repayment: note 21 says conversion needs the approval of the issuer and/or the previous shareholders, management has already repaid Rp25bn of the Rp70bn facility (F26), and the controlling group would not approve a conversion at par that dilutes it by more than half. The terms are NOT undisclosed: note 21 sets the conversion ratio at nominal value, par Rp50 (F27), on the Rp45bn outstanding (F26), so conversion would issue about 900m new shares and take the count from F15's 1,435m to roughly 2,335m, a 63% increase. That dilution is quantified in valuation.bridge as a probability-weighted cost, and it is the bear-case balance-sheet event; it is not hidden in the share count.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 4.0%: house terminal growth for IDR, below the 5% rent escalation assumed in the explicit period and in line with long-run nominal GDP. It is a going-concern convention: the tower sits on an HGB title expiring 2 December 2041 (F18) and the LK states the expiry but discloses no extension premium, renewal cost or management intent, so the perpetuity implicitly assumes renewal at no explicit cost. The exposure is bounded by the DCF weight of 30% - the primary RNAV values the land and the capitalised income without a horizon - and section four states the convention rather than implying a title renewal the LK does not evidence. Sources: S14.

challenges.challenge: Occupancy is stated as 'close to 0.9%' in the summary, s1, s2, s3, s5 and s7, and F16 is stored as 0.9 pct. S2 says 'Tingkat okupansi gedung Rockfields telah mencapai hampir 90 persen' - the quote says the opposite of the claim. The same 90% is the stated support for the two least conservative inputs (cap rate 6.0% and RNAV discount 60% at the top of the band).
challenges.answer: F16 restated to 90.0 pct with the S2 quote (hampir 90 persen) and every section re-rendered; the cap-rate and RNAV-discount justifications were re-read against the corrected occupancy.

challenges.challenge: The load-bearing regime facts - IHSG exclusion from 13 Nov 2026, removal from LQ45/IDX30/IDX80, MSCI freeze and Standalone consultation, and ROCK's 20.0% registry float - are cited [S0, S15]. S0 is a Yahoo statements/price feed with no archived text; S15 is a Kompas article of 5 Aug 2026 about the HSC list reaching 53 names that contains no mention of ROCK, IHSG, LQ45, IDX30 or IDX80 (grep returns zero hits for IHSG). The dated facts exist in the konglo registry (S26/S27) but are not cited.
challenges.answer: Regime facts now cite the exchange and index notices: S16 for the 13 Nov 2026 IHSG removal, S18 for the new HSC methodology and list size, S17 for the MSCI freeze and Standalone consultation, S19 for the raised free float; S0 is cited only for the IDX-IC float and S7 for the HSC concentration.

challenges.challenge: There is no float or turnover math. The datapack shows 3-month ADTV of Rp0.58bn/day against a Rp2.86tn market cap (0.02% of cap per day), so a 10% position needs about 490 days of total volume, while the report carries a 20.0% registry float as 'compliant' and a 10% liquidity discount. The same register is described in F20 as 99.85% held by a group of investors, and no holder above 5% is named.
challenges.answer: Added the float and turnover math: ADTV against market cap, months of full daily volume for a hundredth of the company and more than a year for a tenth, the F20 99.85% concentration against the 20% registry float, and the absence of any named holder above five per cent; the 10% liquidity discount is retained and explained.

challenges.challenge: Forty per cent of the fundamental value is own-history market multiples - P/E 58.34x giving 1,062 and P/BV 1.08x giving 634 - which the report itself calls 'a regime price, not a fundamental one'. The konglo lens then prices the regime premium on top, so the premium is counted inside the fundamental and again in the lens. On RNAV alone the fundamental is about 481 and the price/value gap is 4.6x, not 3.5x; the target moves from 1,570 to roughly 1,430-1,480.
challenges.answer: Own-history P/E and P/BV now carry zero weight; the blend is RNAV 70% and rent-roll DCF 30%, both non-market. The multiples are shown as market context only, and the target is reported under the new construction (RNAV 378, DCF 483, blend 418).

challenges.challenge: The 6.0% cap rate is the lowest in the PROPERTY_DEVELOPERS comp set on an identical engine base (rec_rev x gross margin / cap): MKPI 7.5%, RDTX 8.5%, ARGO 9.0%, JRPT 12.4%, CTRA 14.8%. The '9% on pre-depreciation NPI' conversion is a private basis the peers do not use, so it is not a like-for-like defence. At 8.5% the investment property falls from 1,232 to 869 and RNAV from 478 to about 377 (-21%).
challenges.answer: Cap rate raised from 6.0% to 7.5%, the top of the like-for-like office peer set on the engine identical post-depreciation base; the private pre-depreciation conversion is dropped as not like-for-like. Investment property and RNAV fall accordingly.

challenges.challenge: The development book - 397.3bn of investment property under development plus 49.3bn of land - enters RNAV at full carrying cost with no haircut, and no scenario haircuts it. The property card requires a stated land-bank haircut and warns that undiscounted values are promoter math; s3 itself concludes the paused project 'is worth less than the book'. The largest discretionary asset (26% of RNAV) is never shocked.
challenges.answer: The development book (397.3bn IPUD plus 49.3bn land) now enters RNAV at a stated 30% haircut to cost, sourced to the paused construction, the company own impairment and the F21/F25 land cross-check; the bear case also widens the RNAV discount on that already-marked book.

challenges.challenge: Note 21 says the 70bn zero-coupon convertible with PT Pohon Berkat Gemilang 'has a conversion clause into new shares on the maturity date' (30 Dec 2026); the report calls the terms undisclosed and assumes settlement at par with no dilution, and share_change is 0.0 in every year and every scenario although s5 rates conversion 'high impact'. The bear narrative assumes repayment from cash, so the risk the report names is absent from the bear.
challenges.answer: Par conversion is now quantified: 900m new shares on 1,435m (+63%), more than a third of per-share asset value, carried as a probability-weighted -283bn bridge item at 40% probability while the base case assumes repayment. The terms-undisclosed statement is removed.

challenges.challenge: There is no business bull case. Land and development rights are carried only at cost even though F21 (Jakarta land at Rp16.2m/sqm) is in the pack, no sale or REIT of Noble House is valued, and F17's 495,700 sqm of developing floor area is dismissed as 'not a land bank' without a number. The bull 872 is a regime case, so the report never tests the asset value the company actually owns.
challenges.answer: Added a business bull case: the Rasuna Said restart with a signed tenant, the development book at a stated discount to cost, and F17 explained as floor area rather than land. The bull scenario now mirrors the bear on the same four drivers.

challenges.challenge: The 35% base compression is asserted, not demonstrated, and the report never shows at what compression the return turns non-negative. With ADTV of Rp0.58bn/day a few billion of flow moves this price, and the lens's own bull (25%) is 2,531 above the price. At a compress of 0.09 the target is about 1,970 (flat return), so the rating rests on a 26pp range in a deck parameter that the report treats as fixed.
challenges.answer: Added the compression discussion: the base, bear and bull lens scenarios against the price, the compression at which the return is flat (about a sixth of the log gap), and the named flow events that would justify a smaller compression and make the name a HOLD.

challenges.challenge: The business scenarios are not independent of the regime as the konglo card requires: the bear narrative is MSCI Standalone plus the HSC exclusion sticking, and the bull is MSCI staying in Emerging Markets plus a float increase, so the same regime events are priced once in the fundamental and again in the konglo scenarios. The bull also treats a free-float step as bullish, while the deck's flag logic raises the compress when a float step falls due inside the window.
challenges.answer: Business scenarios now contain only business drivers (growth, gross margin, cap rate, RNAV discount); MSCI, HSC and index events sit solely in the konglo lens. The bull float step is reframed: the deck flag logic raises compression when a float step is due, so it speeds the premium closing rather than preserving it.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E EBITDA margin is 51.7% against 54.5% in FY2025A, a 2.8pp gap, driven by a 50.5% gross margin vs 52.4% actual. The only support is a 9M-2026 ratio whose 9M-2025 comparative is not shown, so seasonality is untested. There is no qc_justifications block in fund record (grep count 0) and the konglo.overlay WARN returns justified:false.
challenges.answer: FY2026E gross margin now shows the seasonality basis (9M-2026 ratio plus the Q4 uplift FY2025 delivered, with the 9M-2025 comparative) and qc_justifications entries are added for weights.changed and konglo.overlay; the calibration gap is now 1.6pp. Re-run confirmed no BLOCK flag.

challenges.challenge: s5 states the scenario probabilities as base 0.5, bear 0.3, bull 0.2 and calls them 'the engine's house weights'; fund record sets 0.45/0.30/0.25. Recomputing the weighted value on the s5 weights gives 699, not 708, and a target of about 1,552, not 1,570.
challenges.answer: Section 5 probabilities now render from the assumptions (45/30/25) and are labelled the analyst own, not the engine weights; the konglo lens scenarios are described as the deck own weights.

challenges.challenge: The premium ratio is misdescribed. 3.51x is the 12-month-forward price (1,995 x 1.1192 = 2,233) over the 12-month fundamental of 637; the spot ratio is 3.13x. The summary and s4 say the shares 'sit at 3.5x' the fundamental, overstating the gap by 12%. s4 also states the compression fractions as 0.3 base, 0.8 bear and -0.1 bull, while the engine used 0.35, 0.75 and -0.10.
challenges.answer: Premium now defined as price over value today (5.34x against v_fundamental), with the twelve-month fundamental stated separately, and the compression fractions are rendered exactly as the engine computes them (35% base, 75% bear, -10% bull).

challenges.challenge: s1 says the revenue note 'splits the year into office rent 136 IDR bn, service charge, utilities...', making the largest line equal to total revenue. Office rent is Rp82.883bn of the Rp136.119bn total (note 27, per the analyst's own params_basis).
challenges.answer: Section 1 now states office rent as F24 (Rp82.9bn) of the Rp136.1bn total instead of equating it with total revenue.

missing_bull_case.note: No business bull case: land and development rights enter only at cost (F21 Jakarta land price sits unused in the pack), no sale/REIT of Noble House is valued, and F17's 495,700 sqm of developing floor area is dismissed without a number; the bull 872 is a regime case.

assumption_realism.note: Cap 6.0% sits 20-30% below the office peers on the same engine base (MKPI 7.5%, RDTX 8.5%, ARGO 9.0%); the 446.7bn development book enters at carrying cost with no haircut; 40% of the fundamental is a 58.3x own-history P/E the report itself calls a regime price.

conservatism_audit.note: Below last actual: FY2026E gross margin 50.5% vs 52.4% (9M ratio used as a full-year rate, no qc_justification) and terminal growth 4% vs 5% escalation. Above evidence: cap 6.0%, no land haircut, 60% RNAV discount at the tight end, 10% liquidity discount against 0.02%-of-cap daily turnover. The stack leans optimistic on the two biggest levers.

signoff.notes: Initiation SELL, target Rp1,440 vs Rp1,995. Facts and lint PASS, no blocking gates, every material question answered on substance. Method set is right for the asset: no presales exist, so RNAV 70% on the tower cap rate plus a 30% rent-roll DCF is correct, and the own-history P/E and P/BV correctly carry zero weight because a triple-digit multiple on a no-growth rent roll with no dividend is a regime price. Cap rate now like-for-like on post-depreciation gross profit at 7.5%, the top of the MKPI/RDTX/ARGO set, and the 30% haircut on a paused, unappraised development book is grounded in the company impairment and the Jakarta land cross-check. Convertible dilution disclosed as a probability-weighted bridge item with the RNAV leg not carrying it; the rating holds on either treatment. Konglo check PASS: no covered siblings in the batch, HSC and float facts sourced, overlay parameters left to the konglo deck. The industry default weights the multiples at 40%, but on this name they are prices of the same stock in the same konglo regime, so weighting them into the fundamental would embed the premium that the konglo lens then prices explicitly (F20, S18, S17). flags.message: konglo lens: price is 5.34x fundamental value (premium); the base case closes 35% of the log gap in 12 months (hsc); target 1,440 vs fundamental 12-month value 418 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The premium is the concentrated-ownership regime, not an earnings anomaly: 99.85% of the register is held by a group (F20), HSC names were removed from the IHSG calculation from 13 November 2026 (S16) and MSCI froze increases while it consults on Standalone status (S17). The lens closes only part of the gap in twelve months because the index demand cannot return while the exclusion holds; the fundamental value is built on the RNAV and the rent-roll DCF alone, with no market multiple inside it.
